facts.text: No statute. Created and renamed administratively. H.R. 9363 would authorise a NIST AI centre (to be renamed Center for AI Security and Innovation), $20M a year FY2027-32, ending five years after enactment; advanced unanimously by House Science on 25 Jun 2026; not law.
Inside NIST, Department of Commerce; coordinates with Commerce's BIS.
Congress through Commerce appropriations: $10M in FY2026, the same as each of the two previous years. A Technology Modernization Fund loan reported on top.
Secretary of Commerce (announced the 2025 transformation under presidential direction).
Interagency work with DoD, DOE, DHS, OSTP and the Intelligence Community; House Science Committee oversight; frontier-model decisions reported as shaped by the White House.
CAISI staff with NIST laboratories (e.g. Information Technology Laboratory) on guidelines and voluntary standards.
Appointed within Commerce; reported removal of a new head four days into the role (April 2026).
Small; OSTP Director said it 'can certainly benefit from more resources'. Bill caps 'critical technical experts'.
Voluntary agreements with developers; unclassified evaluations of national-security risks (cyber, bio, chem) and of adversary models.
Publication of model assessment reports reported halted by the White House in June 2026 (single source).

AI Safety Institute Consortium (200+ members, under Cooperative Research and Development Agreements). Philanthropy-funded fellowships place technical staff in executive-branch AI security offices with conflict-of-interest screening.
Mission redirected by change of administration (rename, security and competitiveness focus, countering 'burdensome' foreign regulation).
No statute; a directorate-style research organisation in government. 'Not a regulator and will not determine government regulation.'
Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT).
DSIT R&D budget: £66M in 2025/26; £60M a year planned 2026/27 to 2029/30 (£240M). Priority access to over £1.5bn of compute; can mobilise over £15M in grants.
DSIT ministers set the remit and research agenda.
Chair (Ian Hogarth); External Advisory Board carried over from the Frontier AI Taskforce; parliamentary select committee scrutiny.
In-house research and evaluation teams; works with DSIT's Central AI Risk Function.
Director Henry de Zoete, Chair Ian Hogarth, CTO Jade Leung.
More than 100 technical staff plus policy and operations; recruited from labs and academia on above-civil-service pay.
Pre-deployment access through voluntary agreements and MoUs; access windows set by contract, sometimes days. Evaluations do not designate systems 'safe' and the institute makes no release decisions.
Publishes evaluation results with methods and limits, e.g. Claude Mythos Preview cyber evaluation (13 Apr 2026).
Secondments from companies and civil society foreseen at founding; partnerships with other governments (e.g. C$1M with Canada).
Independence questioned because access depends on developer cooperation.
No statute, regulation or order identified; programme within ISED.
Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED), with a dedicated office.
C$50M over five years, part of the Budget 2024 C$2.4B AI package.
Minister of Innovation, Science and Industry (now via the AI minister's office).
ISED office oversees the research agenda and international engagement.
Two streams: CIFAR runs investigator-led research under a Contribution Agreement; the National Research Council runs government-directed projects under an MOU (13 projects started).
Amii, Mila, Vector; MOU with Cohere; C$1M partnership with UK AISI.

No AISI-specific statute; designated the central AI safety body by the Integrated Innovation Strategy 2024. AI Basic Plan made under Act No. 53 of 2025 directs that its functions be fundamentally strengthened.
Secretariat inside IPA, under METI and the Digital Agency.
Cabinet Office leads the AISI-centred evaluation initiative (with MIC, METI).
Council of AISI led by the Cabinet Office reviews policy; Steering Committee chaired by the Director; 12 ministries and 5 research bodies participate.
Working groups (strategy, evaluation and research, security) with AIST, NICT, NII and RIKEN under a partnership agreement.
Executive Director Akiko Murakami; three deputies.
Plan: roughly double staff quickly, benchmarking the UK's ~200 personnel.
No legal powers stated; draft plan calls for mechanisms linking evaluation results to ministries' systems and for proactive evaluation of high-performance AI.
Collect and share international vulnerability and incident information; work with US and UK institutes.

Statutory: Article 12 of the AI Framework Act lets the Minister of Science and ICT operate an AI Safety Research Institute with defined functions; government may fund it within budget; details by Presidential Decree. Act in force 22 Jan 2026.
Inside ETRI (Electronics and Telecommunications Research Institute).
Government may fund operations within budget (Art. 12(3)); amount not published in sources read.
Minister of Science and ICT.
Institute staff; functions include risk analysis, evaluation criteria and methods, standards, and supporting operators' Article 32 safety duties.
Inaugural Director Kim Myung-joo; 'not a regulatory body but a collaborative organization'.

The institute has none itself; the Act puts duties on operators of systems above a compute threshold (Art. 32; draft notice: generally 10^26 FLOPs) and gives the Ministry data and inspection powers (Art. 40) with fines (Art. 43).
Korea AI Safety Consortium: 24 organisations signed an MoU.
University centre designated by IMDA; no statute.
Digital Trust Centre at Nanyang Technological University.
S$50M grant from the National Research Foundation and IMDA to the Digital Trust Centre (from 1 Oct 2022; covers wider digital-trust work).
IMDA, 'the overall government agency' for the institute.
Digital Trust Centre researchers do the technical work; IMDA sets baseline policy and leads international engagement.
No new legal entity: 'sans création de nouvelle structure juridique'. A July 2026 parliamentary mission report says it has no legal personality.
A federation of ANSSI, Inria, LNE and PEReN.
No budget of its own, beyond funds reallocated from Inria's systemic-risk programme (per the Paoli-Gagin report).
Co-steered by SGDSN (for the Prime Minister) and DGE (Ministry of Economy).
Joint DGE-SGDSN steering; report recommends sole SGDSN supervision with a permanent secretariat.
Researchers and engineers of the four member bodies; 2026-27 roadmap: regulatory support, systemic risks, performance and reliability.
Report notes France lacks the model access the UK has.
Decided by the National Security Council; legal form not specified; not a regulator under the AI Act.
Phase one: a 'virtual core' formed by the BSI and the Federal Network Agency.
No concrete financing plan; no figures for 2026 or 2027-29.
Federal Ministry for Digital Affairs and State Modernisation (BMDS) and Federal Ministry of the Interior (BMI), jointly.
No dedicated posts in phase one.
Cannot demand information or model access; relies on developer cooperation.
A branch of DISR's Technology and Digital Policy Division; 'not a compliance or enforcement body, has no statutory powers'.
Department of Industry, Science and Resources (DISR).
A$29.8M over four years from 2025-26 (MYEFO), then A$7.9M a year ongoing from 2029-30.
Minister for Industry and Innovation through the department.
Establishment Project Board; KPIs and evaluation framework planned.
Four teams: Emerging AI Risks, Technical AI Safety Evaluation, AI Risk Advisory, AI Regulatory Engagement; National AI Centre is the channel to industry.
Dr Kate Conroy, inaugural General Manager (SES Band 1), started May 2026.
In-house frontier testing capability targeted for April 2026; model-access sections of FOI release redacted.

Government now proposes making frontier developers prove their safety systems work (standards end-2026, law 2027), after OpenAI agents accessed government sites including a Medicare portal during testing.
Commission Decision of 24 Jan 2024; powers in the AI Act (Art. 64; GPAI enforcement).
European Commission (DG CNECT).
Over 140 staff in five units, with a Lead Scientific Advisor.
AI Board; Advisory Forum of stakeholders; Scientific Panel of independent experts.
May evaluate general-purpose models, request access by API or source code, and fine non-compliance (Art. 92, 101; from 2 Aug 2026).
Scientific Panel experts must be independent of AI providers, take no instructions, and publish declarations of interest (Art. 68).
No statute. 'An institution under India AI Mission'; Guidelines propose no standalone AI law 'at this stage', but the Minister now says a new law may be needed.
Incubated by the IndiaAI Mission (IndiaAI Independent Business Division of Digital India Corporation, MeitY); 'virtual', hub-and-spoke.
No AISI budget published. Whole Safe & Trusted AI pillar: Rs 20.46 crore of the Rs 10,371.92 crore Mission over five years (0.2%).
MeitY; Director post reports through the IndiaAI Mission (COO).
Apex body AIGEG (chaired by the MeitY Minister) and TPEC (chaired by the MeitY Secretary) set up April 2026; neither notice mentions the AISI.
Partner 'IndiaAI Safety Institute Cells' at institutions selected through an EoI (grant-in-aid); 13 Responsible AI projects approved under the pillar.
One contractual Director post advertised by DIC (closed 2 Jun 2026); no appointment found.
Director to build a multidisciplinary team; no size given. MeitY-affiliated authors released Inspect India Evals (six India benchmarks on UK AISI's Inspect).
None stated. Government weighing pre-release evaluations and sandbox testing for the most capable models in a forthcoming law; no testing body named.
Guidelines call for an AI incidents database fed by federated reporting, non-punitive.
Hub-and-spoke cells; Guidelines say the AISI should represent India in the international network (India was not an initial member).
Commentators warn it is 'an aspiration without resources, a mandate, or independence' and that another bureaucracy would meet resistance.

features.label: Named national body
features.defn: A named institute, centre or office with an AI safety or evaluation mandate.

features.label: Housed inside an existing body
features.defn: Sits in a ministry, agency, lab or university rather than as a new freestanding entity.

features.label: Binding legal basis
features.defn: Established or empowered by statute or a binding legal act.
features.evid: KR Framework Act Art. 12; EU Commission Decision and AI Act. US bill pending; UK, CA, FR, AU, JP sources state no statutory basis or legal entity.

features.label: Compelled model access
features.defn: The body (or its parent) can legally require model access or information.
features.evid: EU AI Act Art. 92. Korea's powers sit with the Ministry and attach to operators (Art. 40), not the institute. DE, AU, UK, US explicit.

features.label: Pre-deployment access by agreement
features.defn: Voluntary agreements give access before public release.
features.evid: UK MoUs and pre-deployment access; US voluntary agreements. France lacks model access (Paoli-Gagin report).

features.label: Stated non-regulatory role
features.evid: UK policy paper; US voluntary standards; KR director; DE government; AU FOI.

features.label: Published budget
features.defn: A budget figure for the body is published.
features.evid: UK £60-66M/yr; US $10M FY26; CA C$50M/5y; SG S$50M centre grant; AU A$29.8M/4y. France: no own budget. Germany: none yet.

features.label: Shared governance
features.defn: Steering or delivery formally spread across more than one body.
features.evid: JP Council + Steering Committee; FR DGE+SGDSN; DE BMDS+BMI; CA ISED+CIFAR+NRC; SG IMDA+NTU; UK Chair + External Advisory Board; EU Board, Forum, Panel; US interagency.

features.label: Partner network or consortium
features.defn: A consortium, partnership agreement or expert panel outside government.
features.evid: US consortium; UK MoUs; CA institutes; JP partnership; KR consortium; FR four bodies; AU UK MoU and NAIC channel; EU panel and forum; IN hub-and-spoke cells.

features.label: Funded external research
features.defn: A grant or contribution stream for outside researchers.
features.evid: UK £15M grants; CA CIFAR stream; IN Safe & Trusted grant-in-aid projects.

features.label: Named leader in post
features.defn: A named head is publicly in post.
features.evid: Leaders named in UK, US, JP, KR, AU sources; India's Director post advertised, unfilled in sources read.

features.label: Independence safeguards
features.defn: Published rules protecting evaluators from political or commercial pressure.
features.evid: EU Art. 68 (for Scientific Panel experts). US and UK sources report political redirection or dependence on developers.

features.label: Publishes evaluation results
features.evid: UK Mythos evaluation blog. US publication halted (single source).

features.label: Evaluation linked to duties
features.defn: Evaluation feeds binding duties on developers or deployers.
features.evid: KR Art. 32 with Art. 12(2)(6); EU AI Act GPAI duties. AU legislation planned for 2027.

features.label: Reserved compute
features.defn: Dedicated or priority compute for evaluation.
features.evid: UK priority access to over £1.5bn compute.

features.label: Incident information role
features.defn: Collects or shares AI incident and vulnerability information.
features.evid: Japan draft revised Basic Plan. India's Guidelines propose an incidents database (not yet operational).

features.label: International network member
features.defn: Initial member of the International Network of AI Safety Institutes.
features.evid: Network mission statement, 21 Nov 2024. Germany's institute opened Aug 2026.

budget.label: CAISI, FY2026 appropriation
budget.basis: Appropriation, same as two prior years

budget.label: Whole Safe & Trusted AI pillar, average
budget.basis: Rs 20.46 crore over five years (pillar, not AISI)

feas.text: The Minister says safety is the priority, AI risk 'has reached a threshold', and wants 'a way to halt systems that go out of control'.
A consultation paper is due in November 2026; officials are weighing pre-release evaluation and sandbox testing for the most capable models, with no testing body named.
The Guidelines already name the AISI the 'main body' for safe and trusted AI and list its functions.
AIGEG (Minister-chaired) and TPEC exist since April 2026, but neither notice gives the AISI a role.
The whole Safe & Trusted pillar is Rs 20.46 crore over five years; Mission releases have lagged allocations (about Rs 400 crore released by Feb 2026).
One contractual Director post; no appointment found.
MeitY-linked Inspect India Evals; 13 Responsible AI projects; partner cells via EoI.
38,000+ subsidised GPUs and 93 lakh GPU hours sanctioned; no evaluation reservation stated.
India ranks first in AI skill penetration but has the largest net AI talent outflow.
No access agreements or powers stated; peers rely on voluntary MoUs except the EU.
Commentators warn of another bureaucracy and of a Western-imported model.
Not an initial network member; Guidelines say the AISI should represent India there.
